div.head: Governmental decree.
div.p: Santiago Gonzalez, field-marshal, constitutional President of the republic of Salvador, considering—

That from the information received in investigating the origin and results of the revolutionary movement which broke out in Cojutepeque on the 9th instant, it is clearly proved that the reactionaries and disaffected to the government plot secretly against the security of the state, especially devoting their criminal labors to the most valuable portions of the republic;

That in the presence of the activity of the enemies of order, of their clandestine operations, and the imminent danger, the procedures consonant to the laws of the republic appear insufficient, and the guarantees established for the worthy citizens have been converted into shields for the evil-doers; and it being the first duty of the government to preserve the established order, to protect the social interests, and to invigorate the principle of authority, the only safeguard of any political community in circumstances as the present, I have thought well, in accord with the wisest and worthiest portion of the community, and in view of Articles 17 (sections 1 and 2) and 98, of the constitution, to issue the following decree:
Article 1. The executive power of the republic will dictate and execute all the measures conducive to the preservation of peace and interior tranquillity, consulting only the public good, and the greatest expedition in the civil and military action.
Article 2. No publication, periodical or otherwise, of whatever description, shall be circulated, unless, beforehand, a copy shall have been submitted to the minister of the interior.
Article 3. The owners or managers of the press who may disregard the previous article shall suffer a fine of from one to two hundred dollars for the first offense, and the office shall be closed upon a repetition.
Article 4. The government assumes, consequently, the responsibility of its actions, for which it will account, with the opportunity, to the national representatives.
Article 5. This decree shall take effect from the date of its promulgation, and shall cease when the circumstances creating it have terminated.

closer.dateline: Given in San Salvador, in the National Palace, the 17th July, 1872.
